issue 5 context
Orphaned in-flight worker must never produce an unbounded wait
A worker state file is a snapshot its dispatcher rewrites every poll. When the
sub-coordinator dies it takes the dispatcher with it, freezing the file at
state=running forever. Trusting that frozen field wedged a real run for 8.5h.
Fresh snapshot (just written) still means "wait" — the fix must not turn every
genuinely running worker into a spurious recovery.
Same file, aged past the staleness bound: the dispatcher that maintains it is
provably gone, so the "running" claim is stale and recovery must be spawned.
A worker that stays demonstrably fresh still may not be waited on forever.
Compaction handoff is budgeted apart from failure recovery
A sub-coordinator that halts on its context budget did what it was told; that
must not consume the (deliberately tiny) failure-recovery budget.
Failure budget is already spent (2/2); the handoff budget is what applies.

main-state.policy: Preserve unknown fields and legacy permissive admission. New plans use explicit strict concurrency policy.

sub-state.policy: Preserve phase, immutable issue base, in-flight agent records, compaction/recovery counters, and review history.

worker-result.policy: Role-specific artifacts; impl/modify require mandatory commit or verified no-op; plan requires valid JSON and nonempty plan.md. Details in assets prompts.

pair-attempt.policy: argv/cwd/process identity/timestamps/deadline/exit status; future ownership requires stronger identity checks.

pool-state.policy: Preserve supervisor PID/start identity, state-file and event/status log references.

usage-ledger.policy: Preserve history/usage counts and provider subscription target balance.

registry.policy: Use maintained packaged registry; aliases, disabled routes, command argv profiles and model catalog remain data.

issue-report.policy: Outcome, files changed, verification, review summary, token/model usage remain compact report source of truth.
